key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches virtual perovskite recipe shortlists for candidates near high-performing measured devices.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize perovskite compositions, device layers, and processing recipes before costly fabrication.
method: Generate device recipes using reinforcement-learning policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support against 890 measured reference devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates were 23–24% for PPO/RPPO versus 2.9% for random sampling and 10% for the strongest baselines.
watch_item: Neighborhood enrichment does not establish experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage; composition-family coverage also falls sharply at stricter similarity thresholds.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
